result.summary:
The feature is done and all tests pass. When a filter value has more than 5 search terms, the issue list (and other lists that use the shared query form), the calendar and the Gantt chart now show a warning and still display the results. The full test suite passes: 6,073 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors, 64 skips. What changed: - `Redmine::Search::Tokenizer` now has a `MAX_TOKENS = 5` constant. `tokens` still returns at most 5 terms, and the new `truncated?` method says when the text had more. Repeated terms and terms that are too short are removed before counting. - `Query#filter_warnings` returns one message per filter whose value was cut. It only looks at filters of type string, text or search with the operators `~`, `*~`, `!~`, `^` and `$`. Warnings do not make the query invalid. - A new helper, `query_filter_warnings`, shows each message as `

`. Rails escapes the terms. Your task text was garbled in the operator list: the last operator was replaced by a copy of the prompt. I assumed it was `$` ("ends with"), the only other operator that splits the value into terms.

acceptance.criterion: A filter value with more than 5 terms shows the warning and the results
acceptance.evidence: Functional tests pass. The issue list shows p.warning with the exact text 'Subject: A maximum of 5 search terms can be used. Only the following terms were used: "issue", "one", "two", "three", "four"' and the issue rows are still listed. The calendar (ul.cal) and the Gantt chart (section.gantt-pane) also show the warning and still render. The terms are escaped: no <b> element appears inside p.warning.

acceptance.criterion: The change is covered by tests
acceptance.evidence: The 19 new tests (tokenizer, query and functional) pass on the final code: 19 runs, 69 assertions, 0 failures. Rubocop reports no offenses on the changed Ruby files.

acceptance.criterion: The existing test suite still passes
acceptance.evidence: `bin/rails test`: 6,073 runs, 31,686 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 64 skips (the skips are tests that need SCM test repositories, which are missing). The full run started just before a small rubocop cleanup in filter_warnings; the 19 new tests were run again on the final code and pass.
